subject: Discovery recap + proposed model-fit sprint and parity gates
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@finexa.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + proposed model-fit sprint and parity gates

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a concrete proposal so we can get momentum: we heard that Finexa needs a generative assistant for customer support triage and short-form financial recommendations (KYC-friendly), with two hard constraints: latency under 400ms p50 in your EU region, and deterministic redaction of any PII before storage.

What we propose next (high level):
- 2-week model-fit sprint: trial 3 open models vs your current proprietary baseline on a focused prompt set (support triage + disclosure-safe advice).
- Acceptance gates: parity on intent classification (>= 95% vs baseline) and non-inferior safety (zero PII leakage in our regression prompts).
- Deliverables: benchmark CSV, sample prompt set, short runbook for monitoring regressions and a recommended rollback policy.

I attached a one-page sprint scope and a starter prompt set (finexa-promptset-v1.txt). Can you confirm the team to include for sprint logistics and whether legal wants to review the scope before we start?

Proposed next steps: if you agree, I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff on Wed and loop in our ML lead.

Thanks,

—
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap + proposed model-fit sprint and parity gates — need recommended models + acceptance gates

Soojin / Aditya —

Thanks for the context. Below is a recommended, pragmatic plan tuned for Finexa’s constraints. I kept it focused so the sprint is lightweight but gives clear parity signals.

1) Models to trial (order of priority):
   - Llama-4o-7B (8-bit quant): strong instruction following, good cost/latency tradeoff for triage.
   - Redstone-13B-q4 (our tuned open repro): higher-quality completions, expect higher latency but better hallucination control.
   - Baseline (Finexa-prop-v1): we will treat this as "gold" for acceptance metrics.

2) Evaluation plan / metrics:
   - Dataset: use Finexa prompt set (you provided) + 200 held-out production-like examples (redacted in their VPC).
   - Metrics: intent F1 (primary), hallucination rate measured by a factuality checkbench (secondary), response latency (p50/p95).
   - Acceptance: intent F1 >= 0.95 * baseline F1 (i.e., within 5% relative) AND hallucination rate <= baseline + 1.5% absolute. Latency must be <= 400ms p50 in their EU region for any open model variant to be considered viable for prod sandbox A/B.

3) Regression monitoring and quality safeguards:
   - During sprint: run daily automated evals against the prompt set and a small online cohort (sandbox). We’ll push alerts on any drop > 3% relative in F1 and create an automatic rollback flag.
   - Post-sprint: recommend a set of 50 seed prompts for continuous monitoring with weekly aggregation. We’ll provide a lightweight webhook + stats digest so Finexa can host telemetry inside their VPC (no raw text leaves unless they opt in).

4) Ops / data residency:
   - We can run the entire sprint with telemetry exported as hashed features and aggregated metrics to avoid raw logs leaving the VPC. For any deeper labeling or debugging, we will request explicit, time-limited access and provide a secure upload flow (S3 presigned in their account or Azure SAS).

5) Deliverables we’ll share at sprint end:
   - finexa-parity-benchmarks.csv (model vs baseline metrics)
   - prompt-set v1 + v2 (refinements after sprint)
   - short runbook for regression alerts + rollback policy (PDF)

Links / references:
- Benchmark runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/open-vs-prop-2027
- Example benchmark CSV (template): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BExampleCSV

Quick note on hallucination: even when intent parity is met, downstream hallucination tolerance for finance is low. If Redstone-13B-q4 meets F1 but shows small increases in hallucination, we recommend keeping it behind a retrieval-augmented policy or a safety filter for disclosures.

I attached a draft parity benchmark export (CSV).

Happy to sync a 15-min call before kickoff to refine the thresholds with Tom.

—
Marissa Cole
Lead Applied ML, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: finexa-parity-benchmarks.csv (csv)

Elena / Tom —

Thanks for the quick responses. Based on Marissa’s recommendations above, here’s a proposed mutual action plan:

Week 0 (prep): legal and infra review sprint scope (Finexa) — confirm VPC telemetry approach and signing of a short mutual NDA for debug logs if needed.
Week 1 (trial run): run offline benchmarks for three variants (Llama-4o-7B, Redstone-13B-q4, Finexa-prop-v1) against the 200 held-out examples. Daily digest to Finexa’s webhook.
Week 2 (sandbox A/B): deploy best open candidate to prod sandbox for 48–72 hours against a small % traffic to validate latency and live signal.

Deliverables: parity CSV, prompt-set-v2, regression-runbook, and a short readout deck. If acceptance gates are met (intent F1 within 5% relative and hallucination tolerances), we’ll jointly propose a rollout plan and cost estimate for Dedicated capacity or Hosted SLA depending on your isolation needs.
